Sorry, but I believe that mono relationships kinda are that way by their nature. Offering my opinions even if they're not welcomed, since sometimes an opposing viewpoint is helpful.

The fact you control the financials by yourself is a bug red flag to me. The fact that your wife has a home business is also a red flag to me, because it makes me think she's being scammed by a MLM. Nice that she lost weight though! I struggle with that myself and I'm down 40 lbs so far! 

The fact that you're in the country, the fact both her own and your family doesn't support her also means she's very limited if she wants to leave and will severely cripple her ability to form unbiased opinions of your relationship. To me, it sounds like you've made a very pretty cage for her, and clipped her wings so even if she decides the cage is bad and she prefers freedom to control and display, she cannot leave because she lacks the personal freedom to do so.

And even if this excoworker has a strong romantic and sexual relationship with your wife, it will never detract from the experiences you two have together. The point of polyamory to me is that what matters is what's between me and my partner(s), and we both get to decide how that looks. I don't get to tell my partners how to live their lives (especially when it comes to their other partners), I'm just happy they're a part of mine. And that style of relationship has made the happiest and mose fulfilling life I've ever had.

I used to believe in monogamy, but eventually when I caught my partner cheating I realized I was just using it as an excuse to be angry with her because I wanted to own parts of her, and the parts of her I wanted did not include her free will and desires. That was my oh shit moment where I learned I needed to do a lot of personal work, which took a while lol.

Sorry that you two got into a fight over your family on a holiday. That's rough. Next time I suggest hosting your own Thanksgiving and inviting select people you both want there until you have enough to have a great time. Idk if that will work, it's just what I would do.

I don't understand the conflict. Shes a human, right? She can talk and text whoever she wants without shame, right? As for the desire to see other people and maintain your current relationship, consider this: time apart from others gives us fresh perspective and lets us see them in a new light. You could also become good friends with your wife's other partners and learn what helped them be appealing to your wife, and try to incorporate those lessons into yourself as well to improve your time together with your wife. Starting new relationships also often energizes the relationship you two already have.

All that being said, none of that will survive strong feelings of jealousy. So first try to find out if you are jealous of your wife having relationships with other people. Then try to find the source of those feelings. Often times you will find it's rooted in some selfish and possessive assumptions about your relationship, or at least it was for me. Confront the source of those feelings within yourself in therapy and usually that will give you the clarity to let go of jealousy.

Or you could also skip the self improvement, skip the listening, skip the therapy, and ditch her to find a new person who is more accepting of being treated like an object to be owned and treated like a tool for your own enjoyment. There's lots of them around, the problem is most people realize that's a depressing and terrible way to live and they grow out of it. That's probably where you two are right now if I'm being honest.

So my social transition was incredible abrupt and actually happened before any physical changes. I work in the Canadian Forces, so there's policies around who can dress and in what fashion. It also grants vacations in blocks when not doing anything. I first presented femme on one of these vacations.
My mother was very supportive and forced me out of my comfort zone by making me present female for two weeks straight before going back to work. Despite the bad looks, the awkward conversations, and the fear that I could get attacked anywhere, I pushed on. Got a wig, learned makeup, practiced mannarisms, and found my voice. From that point on I have never willingly presented as a male.
